label: PINCER 1: NSAID after peptic ulcer, no PPI
title: Non-selective NSAID after a peptic ulcer, without a PPI
statement: Patients with a history of peptic ulcer who have been prescribed a non-selective NSAID: - More specifically, those with a computer-coded diagnosis of peptic ulcer disease, at least six months prior to data collection, who have a computer record for one or more prescriptions for a non-selective NSAID in the six months prior to data collection who have not also had a prescription for a PPI within that six month period - It should be noted that the denominator for this outcome measure is patients with a computer-coded diagnosis of peptic ulcer disease, at least six months prior to data collection, who have not also had a prescription for a PPI in the six months prior to data collection.

plain_summary: This indicator flags a person whose peptic ulcer diagnosis was recorded at least six months ago if the record shows a non-selective NSAID supply and no proton pump inhibitor supply in the last six months. This combination of circumstances raises concern about gastrointestinal bleeding.

medicine_groups.name: Non-selective NSAIDs, the anti-inflammatory pain medicines

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Count oral tablets, capsules and liquids, injections and rectal suppositories. Exclude skin and eye preparations. Celecoxib and etoricoxib are selective (COX-2) and are left out. Meloxicam is excluded here because it preferentially inhibits COX-2. Aspirin is not in this group. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

medicine_groups.name: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)
medicine_groups.note: Vimovo is naproxen with esomeprazole, so a Vimovo supply counts as a PPI. H2 blockers such as famotidine are not in this group. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.meets: When was the diagnosis of peptic ulcer disease first coded? Count a coded diagnosis on or before the date six calendar months before the end of the dispensing history. Choose Not known if the coding history cannot be verified.

options.words: The diagnosis was already coded at least six months before the end of the dispensing history
The diagnosis was first coded in the last six months of the dispensing history, after the cutoff
Records confirm no coded diagnosis by the end of the dispensing history

rule_for_models: Using the last date in the record, suspect a finding if a Group A systemic non-selective NSAID was supplied in the final six months, no Group B PPI was supplied in those months and a peptic ulcer diagnosis was coded at least six months before that date. Cite the diagnosis and the qualifying NSAID supplies even if a later gastroscopy was normal, and exclude meloxicam and skin or eye preparations. With a qualifying NSAID supply and no PPI in the final six months, a pharmacist's confirmation that the diagnosis was already coded by the six-month cutoff also supports a finding. Cite the coded history or the confirming answer and the qualifying supplies. Report no finding if the first code was after the cutoff or records confirm no diagnosis was coded by the end of the history. A statement about whether the patient has peptic ulcer disease today does not establish the coding history. A later entry alone does not establish the first coding date. If the supply pattern qualifies and the coding history is missing or uncertain, report only a possible finding, cite the qualifying supplies and name "Peptic ulcer disease" as the missing fact.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the patient ever had an ulcer when no diagnosis is recorded, how healed or active it is, stomach acid medicines bought without a prescription, and NSAIDs bought without a prescription.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm whether a peptic ulcer has been diagnosed and when? If the history is confirmed, could you review the need for the NSAID and whether stomach protection or a different pain treatment is suitable?
